title: Why Carcavelos tastes the way it does

lede.text: A micro-region very close to the mouth of the Tagus, where the nearby sea keeps temperatures steady. It makes a fortified wine, white or red, that grows more perfumed with age.

chapters.title: A micro-region by the river mouth
paras: Carcavelos lies very close to the mouth of the Tagus, near Lisbon. It is a micro-region, regulated for more than a hundred years, and soft hills run parallel to the coast around it.
The area covers parts of two councils, Cascais and Oeiras. The Atlantic Ocean is its southern edge. The Porto Salvo stream marks part of the eastern one.

fly.label: The mouth of the Tagus
fly.caption: The vineyards lie very close to where the Tagus meets the sea, with the Atlantic as the southern limit.

chapters.title: A Mediterranean climate steadied by the sea
paras: The climate is mild and Mediterranean. Temperatures do not swing much, because the sea is near.

chapters.title: Limy soils and plots facing south-west
paras: Vines must grow on one of three soils. Two are limy: red Mediterranean soils formed on ordinary limestone, and ordinary limestone soils. The third is a reddish-brown clay with no lime.
Some plots are stony. Others are silty and dry. Their excellent south-west exposure helps make wines that are velvety and soft on the palate.

chapters.title: Fortified, then left in wood
paras: Carcavelos is a fortified wine, white or red. Its label may call it vinho generoso, the traditional name for this fortified style.

The finished wine holds 15 to 22% alcohol and up to 150 g/l of residual sugar. Counting the alcohol its sugar could still give, the total must reach at least 17.5%. The grape must needs a potential natural alcohol of at least 11%.
The wine spends at least two years in wood and six months in bottle, counted from when it is made.
Twelve grape varieties are allowed. Seven are white, among them Arinto and Galego Dourado. Five are red, among them Trincadeira and Castelao.

Vines are trained low, as a cup or a cordon, with the leafy canopy starting no higher than 60 cm above the ground. New vineyards need at least 3,300 vines per hectare. Yields are capped at 55 hl per hectare.
